new_statements.quote: p. 13 (diacritic key): "´ over a letter denotes accentuation of the syllable." p. 14: "Bushman words vary according to the tone in which they are spoken. The middle tone is not marked, the high tone is marked by a dash above the line preceding the syllable, the low tone by one below the line, as ¯ha, _hɑ; rising and falling tones are rare, they are marked 'ha and ˎha." p. 3 (N3 paragraph): "...Bushmen, calling themselves !kuŋ or !o !kuŋ. Their speech is very similar to that of the other !kuŋ, but not quite identical. ... The junior members of the western group are dropping the clicks from many words."

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, no statement held by the project for oung1238). The work supplies only a general tone-marking statement covering N3 among all varieties and an accent diacritic convention; it gives no word-stress placement for !O!ung.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bleek treats all the Bushman languages in the book, N3 !O!kung of Central Angola included, as having lexically relevant tone (three level tones, middle unmarked, high/low marked by dashes before the syllable; rising and falling rare), and the N3 forms in the vocabulary carry these tone dashes. The only accent-related content is the orthographic key line that an acute over a letter marks 'accentuation of the syllable'; no rule for where accent/stress falls is given for any language, and nothing prosodic is said specifically about N3. The words 'stress'/'stressed' occur nowhere in the Introduction (scanned search; agrees with the HTRC token counts held earlier).
new_statements.exceptions: none; the statements are general notation conventions for all twelve varieties (S1-S6, N1-N3, C1-C2, H), not per-language rules
new_statements.identity_note: Bleek's N3 = '!o !kung, Central Angola', recorded by her in 1925 along ca. 15 deg S from the Rhodesian border to the Kwelei River (Introduction p. 3); she notes slight east/west dialect variation, Bantu admixture, and click loss among younger western speakers. This is the variety Glottolog files as !O!ung (oung1238), later merged by ISO into [vaj] Northwestern !Kung.
